problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a General Expression for the Zeros of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
examples.problem: Which expression gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right)?$
examples.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\cot x$ are given by

$$
x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right).$ This gives

$$
2x + \dfrac \pi 6 =  \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{n\pi}{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

feedback.problem: Calculate the period of the function $f(x)=7\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{1}{6}x-\frac{\pi }{12}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a function of the form $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D,$ the period is $\frac{\pi }{B}.$

In our case, we have that $B=\frac{1}{6}.$ Therefore, the period is $\frac{\pi }{(\frac{1}{6})}=6\pi .$
